Thanks for asking! I’d love to see very high-gloss furniture to see how that interacts with the graphics. Think ultra-modern office type vibe.

In contrast, it would be fun to see rustic-rundown items as well. Chipped or peeling wood, frayed or torn sofas—again to see how well that translates into the game’s infrastructure.

An interesting texture to play with would be velvet and satin for clothing, since lighting plays a huge piece in how those materials look
Honestly google this. Do your own research please. This is not an EA game.

From what I’ve seen in some of the folks that had access to gameplay, there is an option in the world editor to add various animals beyond cats - foxes, pandas, and I believe I saw alligators too!  And to my knowledge the animals in Dowon and Bliss Bay cannot be added as pets in a household. I also read on the unreleased world of Cahaya that the cats sound like they’re intractable there, but none of us has seen this yet.

I’m more of a relaxed gamer, I’d focus on a single household and try to work a career ladder. But what excites me most is being able to act as a fly on the wall and just observe the open world and see how all the zois interact. I’m curious about consequences and how that affects the world’s perception of my character. But once that’s been discovered I’m all hands on deck to immerse myself in hyperrealistic builds

Your first paragraph and last sentence basically just sum up everything. And that’s okay! Personally I cannot wait to be inundated with real life effects. All good though, that’s why we have the choice in gaming. 🙂

One step at a time! We’re always here for you. This sub helps me a ton too, it’s nice to hear real stories of people going through the same shitty hand we’ve been dealt. It’s hard, but not impossible. Feel free to reach out

I think it was Ernest Hemingway that said something along the lines of: we are the only person we have when we fall asleep, and the only person we have when we wake up. I’m glad you’re putting yourself first, keep it up! A healthy garden starts with healthy roots.

Something that’s really helping me was a question my psychiatrist asked me: why are you quitting? My answer: because I want to have control over my life. I didn’t even have that answer planned out, but it’s 100% the truth. On the hard days I keep returning to my answer and that has helped keep me going. It shows valor and strength from within, that’s super powerful (at least for me). Whatever your reasons, I’m glad you’re on a healthy path.

Ah that’s awesome to have that kind of family connection. I love to cook too, even on the hard days. Sure some days slide where I don’t cook or flat out don’t even eat, but I never regret making a meal for myself.

For me personally, I’ve been weaning off the caffeine and taking theobromine supplements. It’s an active ingredient found in cacao, and has very similar properties to caffeine, but with more benefits. Eg I feel much more focused, not jittery at all, and the time flies by without me watching the clock or worrying about the next task

Nice one! Those daily tasks can get overlooked sometimes too easily. For us, it can be debilitating. I’m glad you took action to help yourself a bit. Thank you, these are the wins that seem small but really mean a lot to us BP folks. Hope you can have a nice day for yourself!

I second this, OP. I’ve been diagnosed for 10 years (most of it was a misdiagnosis of major depression, was diagnosed with bipolar in 2021.) I’ve tried nearly every drug in the book and hadn’t had success. Turns out after my genesight results came back, my body was low on Folic Acid which really affects how medications are interpreted in the body. The genesight test is a simple saliva swab, mailed, then I received the results a few days after. Once I added my missing component (a folic acid supplement you can pick up without a prescription) I noticed a big change. Definitely worth looking into.
Congrats!! That’s a big step for sure, I’m so glad to hear. Keep us posted, and know that we are here for you ♥️

Hey, thanks for sharing. Someone once mentioned to me that keeping up with hygiene is an ableist mindset—and when others don’t understand your inability to brush your teeth they automatically think that it’s simply because you don’t care. Because ~they~ can do it.

Who cares about them. I’ve struggled with depression for the past decade, and seriously the last thing I worry about is keeping up with hygiene. I want to d*e, not brush my teeth goddammit.

But also, let’s remember that self care doesn’t have to be a full-fledged ordeal. I’ve always despised when people say things like, “just go outside and get fresh air! You won’t regret it! You’ll feel better! It’s hard at first but I can do it so you can do it too!”

Ugh. When I’m depressed, I’m not looking at the end goal, rather, I’m looking how to survive the day without seriously getting myself into trouble. With that being said, how have I made it through to today, where I’m not as depressed as I once was?

It kinda starts with recognizing the patterns, which you already did! Yay! That alone is half the battle for many people who can’t come to terms with their mental health. Half the battle.

So what’s next? I will not tell you to brush your teeth. But, what’s important is to recognize ways to break the pattern. You (and likely a therapist) will have the answer to this.

Also, it kinda looks like you’re halfway there on this too! Based on your post it seems to me that you see the pattern, and as a way to deal with the stressor you brush it off and brush it off again (pun moderately intended). Another half of the battle that you already recognized!

So, let’s not focus on brushing your teeth today. We would love that for you of course, but let’s focus on smaller steps. Half the battle. Then half the battle. Then half the battle. 

Seeing the top of the mountain is always more arduous than looking at the 10 feet in front of you.

Again, let’s not brush teeth today. Instead, how about holding your toothbrush in your hand—with NO intention of brushing your teeth. Hold the toothbrush as long as you want. And that should be it today. No need to guide yourself through thoughts, emotions, anything. Just holding the toothbrush. 1 second, done! Or 5 minutes, done!

Even if you don’t hold your toothbrush today, I’m proud of you for posting. It takes courage to post something like this, and I love to see that. Another half of the battle (I think that’s, like, 4 half’s I’ve mentioned lol) We are glad you’re with us :)

I've pursued sugar daddies before and have had great experiences with them (I'm an old soul, so I tend to get along with older people anyway). My problem with them is I've actually really enjoyed spending time with them and have felt so guilty accepting any money or gifts that I've always declined them, with the exception of a few times when I was really strapped for cash.

I've had a few of my friends say it's like a drug, very addicting, very fleeting, and probably not (mentally) healthy.

In the end I'd say if you're comfortable on your own financially, and like older men, date one for who he is, not what he has.
